issues.body: select_open_issue() documents the match as the structured prefix and the round-2 fix guidance called for matching the complete prefix, but the implementation uses `if f"{marker} {key}:" in title`. Thus a noncanonical title such as `note: [marker] suite=x: ...` can still dedupe as though it were the filer's canonical rolling issue. The copied lane/shard selectors and coverage probe use the same containment pattern. Label scoping makes this a limited hardening concern rather than a blocker, and the key-prefix collision itself is resolved.
issues.fix_hint: Use `title.startswith(f"{marker} {key}:")` here and the equivalent `startswith` checks in the changed lane, shard, and coverage selectors; add one negative test with text preceding the otherwise canonical marker/key fragment.
issues.title: Structured title match is not anchored at the start

verdict.summary: Round 2's major key-boundary defect is fixed consistently across all four filers and the coverage alarm probe: matches now require the canonical colon delimiter, and targeted negative tests cover suite, cluster, lane, and shard prefix collisions. The pagination and real-path self-tests pass. One minor hardening gap remains: the helpers describe and test a structured title prefix but use substring containment rather than startswith(), so a manually edited or mislabeled title containing the canonical fragment later in the text could still be selected. This does not block approval because canonical filer-created titles always begin with the fragment and label scoping substantially limits exposure.
